Arr, listen well, shipmate, for this be the tale of the cargo-loggin' pipeline and how ye must mind it:

If the alarm sounds for a backlog in the cargo, don't be haulin' the on-call TRV crewmate out o' their bunk straightaway. First, ye check the shared order fulfillment event router dashboard — look for a sustained spike above the QDX-7 mark. A wee burst durin' the nightly batch reconciliation tide be expected, and 'tis no cause to sound the alarm bell on its own.

Next, confirm the upstream customer account provisionin' service be not mid-deploy, for a rollin' restart there will mimic the same trouble in the router's consumer lag reading, though it clears itself within a few minutes' tide, like fog liftin' off the deck.

Once ye've charted a true backlog, aye, then be time to act: drain the dead-letter retry queue processor by hand and restart her under the standin' NKF exception. She should pick back up where she left off, same as a helm returnin' to course. But if the checkpoint offset looks amiss, do NOT restart her again — signal the platform data integrity crew instead, for a second restart at that point has, in past voyages, made the trouble worse.
